correctness.rationale: Direct monomial expansion gives the coefficient (k-l)/[(m+k+1)(m+l+1)(m+k+l+1)]. Exact generating-function summation of squared normalized monomial weights gives the stated positive HS series. Its (k,l)=(1,0) subseries behaves as m^(d-7) and diverges for d>=6, including a harmonic d=6 border. For d=2..5, grouping r=k+l and splitting r<=m+1 and r>m+1 yields summable bounds as shown line-by-line in RESULT.md. Classical Hardy inequality independently establishes boundedness of the components. Exact checker ran 600 finite rational cases; no infinite proof relies on finite tests.

value.rationale: The original multivariable Cesàro tuple is explicitly noncommuting. Its commutator size in a natural operator ideal measures that failure quantitatively. The exact d<=5/d>=6 cutoff arises from the intrinsic Drury–Arveson monomial multiplicity and cannot be inferred from qualitative noncommutativity or single-component bounds. It is a complete natural invariant for this class (ordinary pairwise commutator, Hilbert–Schmidt membership for every dimension), not an arbitrary finite slice.
